title: Electronics — Chapter 1: A New Design Gig

questions.question: In Chapter 1, what does E-Z Galaxy’s culture assume about PCB design after Old Bob leaves?
options: That PCB design needs a written process, a mentor, and slow review before any fab order.
That experience can move aside for automation, so the job is treated as easy and largely automated.
That only mechanical engineers may open schematic software.
That every board must be built in-house on a drafting table from the sixties.
questions.explanation: Otto welcomes Ian to a place where “experience moves aside for automation.” Coworkers miss Old Bob but cannot describe his process. The culture treats the role as automated and therefore easy — which is the trap.

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: Welcome to E-Z Galaxy where experience moves aside for automation

questions.question: Why does Ian panic before he has even started designing?
options: His credit card was declined at the cafeteria.
Old Bob’s workflow was never written down, so Ian has no process and no mentor to ask.
The company banned all schematic software.
Otto refused to scan him until he passed an ITAR quiz.
questions.explanation: Ian realizes Old Bob likely never documented his workflow. Without process or someone to ask, he is expected to know PCB design he was never taught in university.

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: with Old Bob gone, who will mentor me in PCB design

questions.question: Ian finishes schematic capture and layout overnight using defaults and automatic placement/routing. What is the chapter’s warning?
options: Automated presets always produce flight-qualified avionics boards.
If the software finishes quickly, DFM review is unnecessary.
Automation can make you feel productive while you still lack manufacturing judgment and a real process.
University courses already cover fab notes, stack-ups, and supplier selection.
questions.explanation: The tools pull Ian along; he feels Old Bob–fast. The story shows that speed from defaults is not the same as a sound, manufacturable design process.

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: it was as if Ian had not led the design software, but the software had led him

questions.question: How does Ian choose a board shop for the whiz-bit module?
options: He visits three fabs, reviews stack-up capability, and dual-sources the order.
He Googles a quick cheap fab, picks one on a 4.2-star rating, and asks for the fastest turn.
He sends the design only to SpaceX’s approved AVL after an RFQ.
He waits for a formal DFM review before ordering anything.
questions.explanation: He searches “Quickie-Cheapo PCB fabrication,” picks Etch-O-Matronic on star ratings, and requests the quickest turn — exactly the “cheap and fast” habit his manager praised in Old Bob, without real supplier judgment.

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: He picked one based upon a customer rating of four-point-two stars

questions.question: The fab replies that a DFM review is in process. Ian brushes the acronym aside. What should DFM have meant to him?
options: Design for Manufacturing — checking whether the board can be built reliably at the fab/assembly house.
Direct Freight Manifest — only a shipping label.
Digital File Mirror — a backup of the Gerbers.
Department of Facility Maintenance — building HVAC rules.
questions.explanation: DFM is Design for Manufacturing. Ian has seen the letters but does not understand them — the same gap a technical buyer must not have when talking fab notes and process capability with suppliers.

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: THANK YOU FOR YOUR 24-HOUR, QUICK-TURN ORDER. DFM REVIEW IN PROCESS.

questions.question: According to the Chapter 1 checklist, which question should you ask before taking a PCB design role?
options: Will the company ban industry events so you stay focused?
Does the company give you a sense that your job is valued and appreciated?
Can you skip software training if star ratings look good?
Is sole-source the preferred culture for every board?
questions.explanation: Page 11 asks whether the company culture values the PCB role, whether tools and training exist, whether you are sole or in a group, and whether you can build a professional network.

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: Does the company you wish to work for give you a sense that your job is valued and appreciated?

questions.question: Which electronics categories does the SpaceX sourcing manager own strategies for?
options: Only raw aluminum structural castings.
PCB, PCBA/contract manufacturing, electronic components, and instrumentation.
Only software licenses and cloud spend.
Only office supplies and facilities.
questions.explanation: The posting’s first responsibility is sourcing strategies for PCB, PCBA/CM, electronic components, and instrumentation — the same domains Chapter 1’s fab decision toys with casually.

reference.section: Why the SpaceX posting sits next to this chapter
reference.lecture: Create sourcing strategies for assigned electronics categories (PCB, PCBA/contract manufacturing, electronic components, and instrumentation)

questions.question: What technical reading skill does SpaceX list so you can guide engineering on suppliers and DFM tradeoffs?
options: Only reading marketing one-pagers from distributors.
Reading drawings, fab notes, stack-ups, and BOMs, and understanding manufacturing complexity.
Memorizing stock ticker symbols for semiconductor firms.
Writing firmware for flight computers.
questions.explanation: Preferred skills call out drawings, fab drawings, stack-ups, data sheets, and BOMs — plus avionics manufacturing complexity. That is the literacy Ian lacked when he treated layout automation as enough.

reference.section: Why the SpaceX posting sits next to this chapter
reference.lecture: strong ability to read drawings, fab notes, stack-ups, and BOMs and to understand manufacturing complexity

questions.question: Ian’s story: pick a fab on stars and chase the shortest turn. SpaceX’s posting: how should supplier readiness be judged before NPI and long-term production?
options: Award the PO to whichever shop emails first.
Visit supplier facilities and assess operational capability, financial health, capacity, and risk.
Use only the cheapest quote with no site visit.
Skip assessment if the online rating is above four stars.
questions.explanation: The posting expects facility visits and assessment of capability, financial health, capacity, and risk before awarding NPI and long-term production — the opposite of Ian’s Quickie-Cheapo click.

reference.section: Why the SpaceX posting sits next to this chapter
reference.lecture: Visit supplier facilities and assess operational capability, financial health, capacity, and risk before awarding NPI and long-term production

questions.question: Which statement matches how the SpaceX role splits work with material planners?
options: This seat owns MRP; planners own the supplier contract.
Planners own MRP; this seat owns the supplier, the contract, and the cost.
Neither side looks at the build plan.
Engineering alone places every purchase order.
questions.explanation: The posting is explicit: partner so demand and inventory stay aligned to the build plan — planners own MRP; this seat owns supplier, contract, and cost.

reference.section: Why the SpaceX posting sits next to this chapter
reference.lecture: planners own MRP; this seat owns the supplier, the contract, and the cost

questions.question: Which cost-reduction levers does the posting expect you to execute — not just admire on a spreadsheet?
options: Piece price
Yield
Ignoring obsolescence until the line stops
Dual-source and tooling
questions.explanation: Cost-reduction projects include piece price, yield, tooling, dual-source, and obsolescence — with planning, stakeholders, and updates. Ignoring obsolescence is the failure mode, not a lever.

reference.section: Why the SpaceX posting sits next to this chapter
reference.lecture: Identify and execute cost-reduction projects (piece price, yield, tooling, dual-source, obsolescence)

questions.question: As the supplier interface for RFIs, RFPs, and RFQs, what does the posting say you do with stakeholders?
options: Forward every email to legal and never run a competitive event.
Run RFX with stakeholders and implement the sourcing decision.
Let engineering place POs with no commercial process.
Publish prices on social media for transparency.
questions.explanation: You are the supplier interface for RFI/RFP/RFQ activity: run RFX with stakeholders and implement the decision.

reference.section: Why the SpaceX posting sits next to this chapter
reference.lecture: Act as the supplier interface for all RFIs, RFPs, and RFQs; run RFX with stakeholders and implement the sourcing decision

questions.question: Which supplier KPIs does the posting expect you to define SLAs around?
options: Cost
Quality
On-time delivery, lead time, and responsiveness
Employee cafeteria star ratings
questions.explanation: Collaborate on SLAs/KPIs for cost, quality, on-time delivery, lead time, and responsiveness — then develop and monitor the supply base. Cafeteria ratings are Chapter 1 satire, not a sourcing KPI.

reference.section: Why the SpaceX posting sits next to this chapter
reference.lecture: define SLAs and KPIs for suppliers (cost, quality, on-time delivery, lead time, responsiveness)

questions.question: True or false: mitigating sole/single-source risk and negotiating continuity-of-supply contracts is part of this SpaceX role.
questions.explanation: The responsibilities explicitly include mitigating sole/single-source risk and negotiating contracts for continuity of supply to protect SpaceX interests.

reference.section: Why the SpaceX posting sits next to this chapter
reference.lecture: Mitigate sole/single-source risk; negotiate contracts for continuity of supply and to protect SpaceX interests

questions.question: Which experience path meets the posting’s basic qualifications?
options: Any one-week online certificate with no electronics exposure.
Advanced degree + 3 years, or bachelor’s + 5 years, or 9+ years, in listed fields such as purchasing, operations/supply chain, or technical procurement of PCB/PCBA/components.
Only a PhD in astrophysics with zero supply-chain work.
Only retail store management with no engineering or procurement background.
questions.explanation: Basic qualifications are an advanced degree and 3+ years, a bachelor’s and 5+ years, or 9+ years in engineering, purchasing, negotiation, planning, operations/supply chain, cost control, MPS, or technical procurement of PCB/PCBA/components/instrumentation.

reference.section: Why the SpaceX posting sits next to this chapter
reference.lecture: Advanced degree and 3+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; or bachelor's degree and 5+ years

questions.question: Why does ITAR eligibility appear on this Hawthorne electronics sourcing posting?
options: It is optional flavor text for marketing.
U.S. export regulations require citizenship, permanent residency, refugee/asylee status, or the ability to obtain the required authorizations.
ITAR only applies to cafeteria vendors.
ITAR replaces the need for BOMs and drawings.
questions.explanation: Launch-vehicle electronics work is export-controlled. Applicants must meet ITAR categories (citizen/national, green card, refugee, asylee) or obtain required authorizations.

reference.section: Why the SpaceX posting sits next to this chapter
reference.lecture: To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national

questions.question: If you interview for this SpaceX seat, which answer best connects Chapter 1’s lesson to the job?
options: I would pick fabs the way Ian did: highest stars, shortest turn, skip DFM.
Automation and a credit card are enough; drawings and stack-ups are engineering-only.
I treat PCB/PCBA cost and schedule as inseparable from manufacturability — I read the package, pressure-test supplier process capability, and never confuse tool speed with a qualified supply base.
Sole-source is fine if the piece price looks low this quarter.
questions.explanation: Chapter 1 warns that automation and cheap/fast habits hide missing process knowledge. The SpaceX role exists to bring supplier strategy, DFM literacy, and risk control to exactly that gap.
